A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EdgeClippedGossip research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original gossip simulations on fully connected and modified-torus graphs, including error and bias/heterogeneity results in Figures 1–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original Two Worlds graph simulations comparing global clipping, local clipping and local trimming under Byzantine attacks in Figures 1–2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the Global Clipping Rule and the substantive directed local-clipping procedure are retained. Simplified GCR survives in Appendix B.3. Recasting local clipping/trimming as CS-RG/GTS-RG and attributing Spectral Heterogeneity to prior work does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The synthetic five-dimensional average-consensus task remains, but the fully connected and modified-torus environments are replaced by a Two Worlds graph. ALIE and FOE replace the No Attack and Consensus scenarios; Dissensus and Spectral Heterogeneity remain.

E2.justification: The experimental comparison drops He et al.'s rule-of-thumb local clipping and Simplified GCR, narrowing the five-method comparison to three. Global clipping, the earlier local-clipping rule and local trimming remain, with the latter two identified as CS-RG and GTS-RG.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes from 20 total nodes and 30 communication iterations to 64 honest nodes and 100 iterations. A sweep over Byzantine proportions becomes a sweep over one to five Byzantine neighbors per honest node. Gaussian N(0, I5) initialization and relative MSE remain.

E4.justification: The bias/variance analysis is replaced rather than merely relocated: v1 Appendix A uses a Consensus attack on a clique, while v2 Figure 1 uses ALIE on Two Worlds. The modified-torus failure study and empirical exact-versus-simplified GCR comparison disappear, substantially revising the robustness and supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports averaging MSE over 200 samples; v2 explicitly reports averaging configurations over five seeds. These descriptions do not establish comparable independent-run counts. v2 Figure 2 also introduces shaded bands, but neither its caption nor the experimental description defines their statistical meaning.

E6.justification: The clique and torus results in v1 Figures 1–3 are replaced by Two Worlds results in v2 Figures 1–2. For example, v2 reports GCR relative MSE equal to 1 at four and five Byzantine neighbors while local methods remain below 1. These are changed-setting results, not directly comparable performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 removes the local-clipping/trimming convergence and bias results, including Theorems 4.5 and 4.12, Corollary 4.9 and Appendix B.2 proofs, plus the attack derivations. The global-clipping proofs remain, and Section 4.2 adds mathematical discussion of invariant loss and Lyapunov difficulties. Theorem 1 also introduces a squared-distance cutoff inconsistent with the distance-based clipping definition in Equation (7).

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes novel practical global/local clipping rules, tight guarantees and constructive attack design. v2 drops the attack-design contribution and shifts toward dual derivation, reinterpretation of existing methods and obstacles to extending the framework beyond average consensus.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly characterizes GCR as a proof of concept requiring favorable coordination, acknowledges oracle threshold information and the lack of an asymptotic-error characterization, and explains the invariant/Lyapunov obstacle for general objectives. It also adds a qualification that superiority against individual attacks does not establish greater worst-case robustness.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds implementation formulas for ALIE and FOE alongside the retained Dissensus and Spectral Heterogeneity descriptions. Section 5 newly specifies choosing the largest threshold satisfying GCR. These are focused additions to experimental documentation.

R1.justification: Gaucher et al. (2025) becomes central to the attribution of local clipping, trimming and Spectral Heterogeneity, substantially changing the contribution's positioning. v2 also adds Jakovetić (2018) and Allouah et al. (2023), while removing several earlier consensus and decentralized-robustness references, including Vaidya, Peng and Fang.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Section 2 is reorganized around deriving the dual method, and the former local-convergence and attack sections give way to reinterpretation and generalization difficulties. Appendix A changes from additional experiments to experimental design.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout with substantially different typography and author presentation. The experimental figures are replaced and redesigned with different axes, legends and bands. The related-work comparison table disappears, while the notation table moves from the main text to Appendix B.

improvement.justification: v2 improves calibration by explaining GCR's practical limitations and the structural obstacles to broader optimization. However, it removes self-contained local-convergence analyses and informative comparisons, while introducing a norm-versus-squared-norm inconsistency in Theorem 1. The global proof remains, but these gains and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
